title: Day-1 loop run record — one execution of reflective_task, stored
description: Graph Engineering §VI.A: 'Add: stored first draft, evaluator with explicit criteria, revision step, stopping rule. Store every artifact.' This record IS the storage requirement — one file per loop run, holding every version, every review, the stopping reason, and the quality delta that is the rung's exit criterion ('measured quality improvement', Table II). A loop whose artifacts are not stored cannot be said to have measured anything, so the runner writes this before it reports.

mode.description: selftest = deterministic scoring of the hand-authored reference drafts; NO model was called and this is NOT a measurement of the skill. measure = the real loop against a live model. The two must never be conflated in a report — see the F1 lesson in evals/README.md.

model.description: Null in selftest mode. In measure mode this is required — an unlabeled quality number is not a measurement of anything (same rule the trigger-eval baseline already enforces).

versions.description: versions[0] is the paper's 'stored first draft'; each later entry is one revision step.

reason.description: 'approve' and 'iteration_limit' are the paper's two exits verbatim. 'no_improvement' is an added ratchet stop — §IX.B warns a ratchet optimizes the metric it can see, so a round that fails to move the score is not spent again.

quality.description: The rung's exit criterion, made arithmetic.

improved.description: delta > 0. This single boolean is Day 1's exit criterion for this skill+fixture.

best_score.description: Highest score any round reached. Meaningful only once the artifact is carried between rounds, which makes it possible for a revision to BREAK something an earlier round had working.

regressed.description: final_score < best_score. Reported separately because final_score alone hides it: a run that reached 0.8 and fell back to 0.6 reads identically to one that never got past 0.6. §VIII.B — 'do not hide partial failure behind a fluent final answer.'

cost.description: Null in selftest mode (zero spend by construction). Required in measure mode: §VIII.B insists every run declares and reports its budget. Figures come from the CLI's own `--output-format json` envelope (`total_cost_usd` plus the per-model `modelUsage` block), NOT from tokens multiplied by a price table — a price table in this repo would go stale and produce a confident wrong number. A null here means NOT REPORTED, never zero: if any round failed to report, the run total is withheld rather than published as a partial sum.

tokens_in.description: Uncached input tokens, summed over the session's modelUsage entries. NOT `usage.input_tokens`, which describes only the last assistant message — measured 10 vs 531 on a one-turn probe.

tokens_out.description: Output tokens, summed over the session's modelUsage entries.

usd.description: The CLI's own `total_cost_usd`, summed across rounds. List-price equivalent as computed by the CLI; on a subscription this is not necessarily what was billed.

cache_read_tokens.description: Cache-read input tokens. Priced into `usd` already; reported separately because the session preamble dominates a short round.

source.description: Where the figures came from. `cli-json` is the only value that licenses reading the totals as measured spend. `partial` means at least one round reported and at least one did not — totals are null in that case by design. `unavailable` means none did (e.g. the SKILL_LOOP_CMD override path, whose output format is unknown).

rounds_reported.description: How many rounds reported a cost.

rounds.description: How many rounds ran. rounds_reported < rounds is why a total may be null.

per_round_usd.description: Per-round spend in round order, preserved even when the total is withheld, so the gap is inspectable. A run that cost $4 in one runaway round and one that spread $4 over five are different findings a total cannot separate.

source.description: Provenance of this draft. A reference-* version is hand-authored fixture text; only 'model' is real skill output. Keeping this on the version (rather than only on the run) means a mixed record can never be misread as measured.

artifact.description: Workspace rubrics only. Path to the DELIVERABLE this round produced — the code, not the transcript about the code. `path` stores what the model said; without this, a low score is undiagnosable and the only way to see what was actually built is to pay for the run again.

carried_forward.description: Workspace rubrics only. True when this round started from the previous round's deliverable, false when it started from an empty directory. This is the difference between a revision and a re-roll: with it false, a flat delta means the loop re-sampled the skill rather than iterating on one artifact, and must not be read as 'revision did not help'.

sha256.description: Recomputed by the scorer from the text it actually graded — the same discipline spec-evaluator already applies to a T0 citation.

cost.description: What THIS round cost, as reported by the CLI envelope. Null where the round reported none.

changes.description: The revision instructions fed into the next round. §V's grounding-layer example: a reviewer returns criterion-level required evidence, never 'looks good'.

evidence.description: The matched substring, truncated. A criterion result with no evidence is an assertion; with evidence it is a finding.
